claim_investigated: McKinsey: $95B / 19% of US logistics costs lost at blind handoffs between shippers and carriers
original_source_flagged: transportandlogisticsme.com (trade press) — no direct McKinsey URL

new_sources.key_data: McKinsey analysis finds that between 13 and 19 percent of logistics costs stem from inefficient interactions at handoff points, amounting to up to $95 billion in losses per year in the United States economy alone. The article uses the term 'blind handoffs' explicitly. The full range cited is $65 billion to $95 billion of waste generated at interaction points between shippers, dispatchers, 3PLs, and carriers. B2B interactions account for $45B-$66B/year; B2C $18B-$28B/year. Costs impact carriers most, accounting for 6-13% of carriers' overall revenue.

Note: the trade press rounded to the upper bound ($95B / 19%); the precise McKinsey range is $65B–$95B / 13–19%, so the claim should be widened to the full range rather than citing the upper bound alone.
